[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

[[Category:Oak Grove Cemetery, Lexington, Virginia]]
== Biography ==
Robert was born in 1792, in Rockingham County, Virginia. He was the son of [[Glasgow-649|Arthur Glasgow]] and [[McNutt-600|Rebecca Anderson McNutt]]. 

On 27 Mar 1821, in Botetourt, he married [[Anderson-46490|Catherine Thomas Anderson]]. They settled in Rockbridge and had the following children.
#Margaret Gordon Glasgow b. 1822 - d.  1907, never married
#Joseph Reid Glasgow b. 1823 - d. 1847, age 24
#William Anderson Glasgow b. 1825 - d. 1910, m1/wid. Elizabeth Crisman Spears, m2. Grace Ellen Shanks
#Rebecca Anderson Glasgow b. 1827 - d. 1915, never married
#[[Glasgow-474|Francis Thomas Glasgow]] b. 1829 - d. 1916, m. Ann Jane Gholson
#John McNutt Glasgow b. 1831 - d. 1837, age 6
#Kate Glasgow b. 1835 - d. 1916, m. James Paxton
#Robert Arthur Glasgow b. 1836 - d. 1862, age 26, never married
#Mary Jane Glasgow b. 1838 - d. 1890, m. John Thomas Dunlop

Living in Lexington, Rockbridge throughout his life, it is here he passed away in 1862. He is buried at the Oak Grove Cemetery.


== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-649]] is assessed at 99% (proved). Joseph’s 1831 will calls Robert a son of his deceased brother Arthur and his own nephew. Combined with the Arthur/Rebecca McNutt family account, this identifies the selected Arthur as Robert Arthur’s father.

Direct paternal kinship wording; the will does not itself establish Robert’s mother.

Next useful test: Use the original will if a competing Robert nephew is raised.

Source basis already held: [https://swvirginians.wordpress.com/2014/12/12/joseph-glasgow-pulaski-co-va-will-of-1831/ Wythe County, Virginia, will of Joseph Glasgow, executed 2 April and presented 11 April 1831; earlier published transcription () and RootsWeb transcription]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.
